---
title: Get the data
description: Read OmicIDX Parquet from DuckDB, Python, or R over anonymous HTTPS.
---

```{r}
#| include: false
# Python cells run through reticulate, in a uv-managed environment.
reticulate::py_require(c("duckdb", "polars", "pyarrow"))
```

Every OmicIDX table is a Parquet file under
`https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/`. Anything that reads Parquet over
HTTPS can use it. You don't need an account or a key. There's no REST API.

- **DuckDB:** [Query with DuckDB](duckdb-snapshot.qmd) covers the published database, every table, and example queries.
- **R:** the [omicidxr](r-omicidxr.qmd) package connects in one line and replaces SRAdb and GEOmetadb.
- **In the browser:** the [playground](../playground.qmd) runs SQL with DuckDB-Wasm, nothing to install.
- **Pinning and citing:** [Versions and citation](versions-and-citation.qmd) explains `latest/`, dated folders, and the monthly HuggingFace releases. [Releases](../releases.qmd) lists what's available.

The recipes below use `latest/` and ran when this page was built. Swap in
`v{YYYY-MM-DD}/` to pin a date.

## Python

With [polars](https://pola.rs), `scan_parquet` reads lazily, so only the
columns and row groups a query needs are fetched. To try it without a
project, run `uv run --with polars python`.

```{python}
#| jupyter_compat: true
import polars as pl

base = "https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest"

studies = (
    pl.scan_parquet(f"{base}/sradb/study.parquet")
    .filter(pl.col("study_type") == "Transcriptome Analysis")
    .select("study_accession", "study_title")
    .head(10)
    .collect()
)
studies
```

With [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/docs/api/python/overview), attach the
published database and get a polars frame back. `.pl()` needs
[pyarrow](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/python/) installed, so run it with
`uv run --with duckdb --with polars --with pyarrow python`:

```{python}
#| jupyter_compat: true
import duckdb

con = duckdb.connect()
con.sql("ATTACH 'https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/omicidx.duckdb' AS omicidx (READ_ONLY)")
gsms = con.sql("SELECT gsm FROM omicidx.geometadb.gse_gsm WHERE gse = 'GSE118849'").pl()
gsms.head()
```

## R

The [omicidxr](r-omicidxr.qmd) package connects for you, pins a
version, and has SRAdb- and GEOmetadb-style helpers:

```{r}
library(omicidxr)

con <- omicidx_connect()
gsms <- geo_samples(con, "GSE118849")
head(gsms[, c("gsm", "title", "gpl")])
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
```

Without the package, [duckdb](https://r.duckdb.org) gives you the same
database through DBI:

```{r}
#| message: false
library(DBI)

con <- dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())
dbExecute(con, "INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;")
dbExecute(con, "ATTACH 'https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/omicidx.duckdb' AS omicidx (READ_ONLY)")

gsms <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT gsm FROM omicidx.geometadb.gse_gsm WHERE gse = 'GSE118849'")

# Any table, without the database
dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT count(*) AS n
  FROM read_parquet('https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/sra_studies.parquet')
")

dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
```

## Command line

```bash
# Row counts for every published table
curl -s https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/manifest.json

# One table, downloaded
curl -O https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/geometadb/gse.parquet
```
